findings.title: [P1] Validate every find root before granting the rm exception
findings.body: The new expression captures only the first root and silently consumes additional roots before `-exec`. A command such as `find <permitted-root> <protected-root> -exec rm -rf {} \;` therefore receives the same `_seg_find_root` as the permitted single-root command, although `find` executes the deletion against both trees. The previous root-count check explicitly rejected this case. Restore rejection of multiple roots, or validate every root before granting the exception, to prevent bypassing the destructive-command guard.

findings.description: The find-root resolution for `find ROOT ... -exec rm ...` was weakened. The old code tokenized everything between `find` and `-exec`, stopped at the first flag/predicate token, and set `_seg_find_root=""` (the conservative 'unknown root' value) unless EXACTLY one root token was present. The new regex `find[[:space:]]+([^;&|)[:space:]]+)[^;&|)]*-exec$` captures only the FIRST whitespace-delimited token and line 807 assigns it unconditionally. Two previously-conservative cases now yield a wrong, non-empty root: (1) multiple roots, e.g. `find /tmp/scratch / -exec rm -rf {} \;` resolves root to `/tmp/scratch` and silently ignores `/`; (2) flags before the root, e.g. `find -L / -exec rm -rf {} \;` or `find -depth / -exec rm -rf {} \;` resolves root to the literal string `-L`/`-depth`, which will never match any protected-path list. The in-diff comment claims the flag-first case 'keeps today's conservative behavior', but the code no longer produces the empty root that conservative behavior relied on. Downstream consumption of `_seg_find_root` (the `{}` substitution / protected-path check) is outside the shown hunk, so I could not confirm the exact allow/deny outcome, but any logic that treats a non-empty root as the resolved `{}` target will now evaluate the wrong path.
findings.failure_mode: An agent-issued (or prompt-injected) command such as `find -L / -exec rm -rf {} \;` or `find ./tmp / -exec rm -rf {} \;` passes the destructive-bash hook because the root used for the protected-path check is `-L` or `./tmp` rather than `/`, and the recursive delete runs against the filesystem root or home directory.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the single-token regex but restore the guard: reject group 3 when it starts with `-`, `!`, `(`, `)` or `\` (set `_seg_find_root=""`), and re-scan the remaining span `[^;&|)]*` for additional non-flag tokens; if more than one root is present, set `_seg_find_root=""` so the conservative path is taken. Add fixtures for `find -L / -exec rm -rf {} \;`, `find -depth / -exec rm -rf {} \;`, and `find /tmp / -exec rm -rf {} \;` asserting BLOCK. Update the comment so it no longer claims flag-first keeps conservative behavior.

findings.description: `for dir in ${sprint_dirs}` iterates unquoted `find` output, so paths undergo word splitting and pathname expansion. A grimoire path or `sprint-*` directory name containing whitespace or glob metacharacters is split or expanded, producing wrong counts (or, with `set -u`/`-e`, aborting the script). Separately, the count is no longer bounded by `get_total_sprints`; any `sprint-*/COMPLETED` present under `a2a/` (e.g. `sprint-99`, stale dirs from a previous cycle) counts, so `completed >= total` can be satisfied without sprints 1..N being done. `determine_state` then reports `complete` and `suggested_command` becomes `/deploy-production`, which downstream agent automation consumes.
findings.failure_mode: Repository content (a stray or attacker-committed `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-X/COMPLETED` file) flips workflow state to `complete`/`deploy-production` even though real sprints remain unreviewed/unaudited, and odd directory names cause miscounts or script failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `find ... -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' dir` or a quoted glob array (`for dir in "${a2a_dir}"/sprint-*/`), and only count directories whose numeric suffix is within 1..total from `get_total_sprints` (or revert to the bounded loop).

findings.description: Removal of `_is_billing_class_error` means HTTP 4xx responses caused by account-side conditions (credit balance exhausted, invoice overdue, billing disabled, insufficient quota) are now raised as terminal `InvalidInputError` in both the streaming and non-streaming paths rather than `ProviderUnavailableError`. The retry/fallback layer will therefore stop instead of chain-walking to the next configured provider. No secret exposure is introduced (messages still pass through `sanitize_provider_error_message`), but availability under billing failures regresses.
findings.failure_mode: When the Anthropic account hits a quota/billing block, every request fails terminally instead of failing over to an alternate provider, causing an outage of the agent pipeline until an operator intervenes.
findings.suggested_fix: If the intent is to retire the substring heuristic, replace it with classification on the structured `error.type` field (e.g. `permission_error`/`billing_error`) rather than dropping fallback entirely; otherwise restore the billing-class routing.
